skills.subject: reading
skills.title: Story: The Day the Sun Slept In
skills.activity: Read a farm story, then play games about it. Stars Bodhi and Kona the dogs!
skills.parentTip: Read it together first. This one story covers all the Kindergarten reading skills.
skills.teach: Read a farm story, then play games about it. Stars Bodhi and Kona the dogs!

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Counting Critters
skills.activity: Count, compare, and find out how many with the Counting Critters!
skills.parentTip: Covers all the Kindergarten counting and comparing skills.
skills.teach: Count, compare, and find out how many with the Counting Critters!

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Gabriel's Family of 10
skills.activity: Add and take away with Gabriel's 7 cats, 2 dogs, and 1 Gabriel!
skills.parentTip: Addition and subtraction to 10, built on the family of 10.
skills.teach: Add and take away with Gabriel's 7 cats, 2 dogs, and 1 Gabriel!

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Sort the Farm Animals
skills.activity: Sort the chickens, sheep, cats, and dogs into their groups, then count how many are in each!
skills.parentTip: Sorting into categories and counting each group. Uses our real farm: lots of chickens, just a couple of dogs.
skills.teach: Sort the chickens, sheep, cats, and dogs into their groups, then count how many are in each!

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Shape Detective
skills.activity: Find the circle, square, triangle, rectangle, and hexagon by name or by how many sides!
skills.parentTip: Naming and describing flat shapes. He learns each shape's name and its number of sides.
skills.teach: Find the circle, square, triangle, rectangle, and hexagon by name or by how many sides!

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Shape Spotter
skills.activity: Find every triangle, even the small or turned ones! Spot each shape no matter its size or which way it faces.
skills.parentTip: Naming shapes regardless of size or orientation. A triangle is still a triangle when it is tiny or rotated.
skills.teach: Find every triangle, even the small or turned ones! Spot each shape no matter its size or which way it faces.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Build a Shape
skills.activity: Put shapes together to make a picture! A triangle and a square make a house. Tap the missing shape to finish each one.
skills.parentTip: Composing simple shapes into a bigger shape. At home, build pictures from blocks or cut-paper shapes together.
skills.teach: Put shapes together to make a picture! A triangle and a square make a house. Tap the missing shape to finish each one.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Where Is It?
skills.activity: On top, under, or next to? Tap the picture that matches the words!
skills.parentTip: Position words. Narrate them at home: the cat is ON the chair, the ball is UNDER the table.
skills.teach: On top, under, or next to? Tap the picture that matches the words!

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Count the Legs!
skills.activity: Count the animal's legs and tap the number! A bird has 2, a dog has 4.
skills.parentTip: Counting to tell how many. Count the legs on your real animals together.
skills.teach: Count the animal's legs and tap the number! A bird has 2, a dog has 4.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Make 10
skills.activity: Some animals are here. Tap how many MORE make 10!
skills.parentTip: Making ten with a missing part. Practice on fingers: 6 and 4 more make 10.
skills.teach: Some animals are here. Tap how many MORE make 10!

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Take Away
skills.activity: Some animals hop away. Count how many are LEFT!
skills.parentTip: Subtraction within 10 by taking away. Act it out with toys or snacks.
skills.teach: Some animals hop away. Count how many are LEFT!

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Doubles
skills.activity: Double it! 2 and 2 more makes 4. Tap the total!
skills.parentTip: Doubles facts — quick building blocks for adding. Say them like a chant.
skills.teach: Double it! 2 and 2 more makes 4. Tap the total!

skills.subject: math
skills.title: First, Second, Third
skills.activity: Who is first, second, third? Count from the front and tap it!
skills.parentTip: Ordinal numbers. Line up toys and name their places together.
skills.teach: Who is first, second, third? Count from the front and tap it!

skills.subject: reading
skills.title: Beginning Sounds
skills.activity: Which animal starts with that letter? Tap the matching sound!
skills.parentTip: Letter-sound matching. Say the animal's name slowly: b-b-bear.
skills.teach: Which animal starts with that letter? Tap the matching sound!

skills.subject: science
skills.title: Growing Up
skills.activity: Living things grow and change! Tap what comes next.
skills.parentTip: Life cycles. Talk about how your animals grow from babies.
skills.teach: Living things grow and change! Tap what comes next.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Count by 10s
skills.activity: Ten, twenty, thirty... tap what comes next when you count by tens!
skills.parentTip: Skip counting by tens. Count in groups of ten together.
skills.teach: Ten, twenty, thirty... tap what comes next when you count by tens!

skills.subject: science
skills.title: Fast or Slow
skills.activity: Is the animal fast or slow? Tap to sort it!
skills.parentTip: Comparing how things move. Talk about fast and slow animals you know.
skills.teach: Is the animal fast or slow? Tap to sort it!

skills.subject: science
skills.title: Sink or Float
skills.activity: Will it sink or float? Tap your guess!
skills.parentTip: Predicting sink or float. Try it in the bath or a bowl of water together.
skills.teach: Will it sink or float? Tap your guess!

skills.subject: reading
skills.title: Big & Little Letters
skills.activity: Find the little letter that matches the big one!
skills.parentTip: Matching uppercase and lowercase. Point them out on signs and books.
skills.teach: Find the little letter that matches the big one!

skills.subject: science
skills.title: Five Senses
skills.activity: See, hear, smell, taste, touch — tap the part you use!
skills.parentTip: The five senses. Name which sense you're using during the day.
skills.teach: See, hear, smell, taste, touch — tap the part you use!

skills.subject: reading
skills.title: Opposites
skills.activity: What's the opposite? Big and little, hot and cold!
skills.parentTip: Opposite words. Play an opposites game while you walk or cook.
skills.teach: What's the opposite? Big and little, hot and cold!

skills.subject: science
skills.title: Animal Homes
skills.activity: Where does each animal live? Farm, ocean, cold places, or jungle. Tap the one that fits!
skills.parentTip: Animals and where they live. Talk about where your farm animals live vs. ocean or jungle animals.
skills.teach: Where does each animal live? Farm, ocean, cold places, or jungle. Tap the one that fits!

skills.subject: science
skills.title: Fur, Feathers, Scales
skills.activity: Is it covered in fur, feathers, or scales? Tap the animal that matches!
skills.parentTip: Animal body coverings. Feel your animals' fur and feathers together.
skills.teach: Is it covered in fur, feathers, or scales? Tap the animal that matches!

skills.subject: science
skills.title: What Do Animals Eat?
skills.activity: Every animal eats! Tap the food each animal likes to eat.
skills.parentTip: What animals need to live. Talk about what you feed your animals each day.
skills.teach: Every animal eats! Tap the food each animal likes to eat.

skills.subject: reading
skills.title: Syllable Safari
skills.activity: Tap each beat of the animal's name and clap it. Then count the claps!
skills.parentTip: Breaking words into syllables. Clap names together — RAB-BIT, EL-E-PHANT.
skills.teach: Syllables are the beats in a word. Clap as you say it: el-e-phant has 3 claps!

skills.subject: science
skills.title: Animal Groups
skills.activity: Mammal, bird, fish, reptile, or bug? Tap the group each animal belongs to!
skills.parentTip: Sorting animals into groups by their traits (fur, feathers, scales, fins, six legs).
skills.teach: Animals come in groups: mammals have fur, birds have feathers, fish have fins, insects have 6 legs.

skills.subject: science
skills.title: Animal Sounds
skills.activity: Moo, woof, quack! Tap the sound each animal makes.
skills.parentTip: Animal sounds. Make the sounds together and guess the animal.
skills.teach: Every animal makes its own sound. A cow says moo, a duck says quack, a sheep says baa.

skills.subject: science
skills.title: Four Seasons
skills.activity: Spring, summer, fall, or winter? Tap the season that matches the picture.
skills.parentTip: The four seasons and their weather. Talk about what changes each season.
skills.teach: The year has 4 seasons: spring flowers, hot summer, falling leaves in fall, and cold snowy winter.

skills.subject: science
skills.title: Swim, Fly, or Walk?
skills.activity: Does the animal swim, fly, or walk? Tap how each one gets around!
skills.parentTip: How animals move. Point out swimmers, fliers, and walkers when you're outside.
skills.teach: Animals move in different ways. Fish swim, birds fly, dogs walk. How does each one get around?

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Count by 5s
skills.activity: Count by fives! 5, 10, 15... Tap the number that comes next.
skills.parentTip: Skip counting by 5s. Count hands and fingers together — 5, 10, 15.
skills.teach: Counting by 5s is like counting hands: 5, 10, 15, 20. It's a quick way to count.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Count by 2s
skills.activity: Count by twos! 2, 4, 6... Tap the number that comes next.
skills.parentTip: Skip counting by 2s. Count pairs — eyes, ears, socks — 2, 4, 6.
skills.teach: Counting by 2s skips every other number: 2, 4, 6, 8. It's faster than counting by ones!

skills.subject: reading
skills.title: Baby Animal Names
skills.activity: A baby dog is a puppy! Tap the special name for each baby animal.
skills.parentTip: Animal vocabulary. Quiz each other on baby animal names.
skills.teach: Baby animals have special names. A baby dog is a puppy, a baby cat is a kitten, a baby cow is a calf.

skills.subject: science
skills.title: Parts of a Plant
skills.activity: Roots, stem, leaves, or flower? Tap the part that does each job!
skills.parentTip: Parts of a plant and their jobs. Look at a real plant together.
skills.teach: A plant has parts with jobs: roots drink water, the stem holds it up, leaves catch sun, the flower makes seeds.

skills.subject: science
skills.title: Hot or Cold?
skills.activity: Fire, ice, sun, snow — tap whether each thing is hot or cold!
skills.parentTip: Temperature — hot vs cold. Point out hot and cold things at home.
skills.teach: Some things are HOT, like the sun and fire. Some are COLD, like ice and snow. Be careful with hot things!

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Teen Numbers
skills.activity: A teen number is ten and some more! Count the ten plus the extras and tap the number.
skills.parentTip: Teen numbers as ten and ones. Build 10 with objects, then add a few more.
skills.teach: A teen number is ten and some more! Count the ten plus the extras and tap the number.

skills.subject: science
skills.title: Baby Animals
skills.activity: Baby animals look like their parents! Find each animal's baby.
skills.parentTip: Young animals resemble their parents. Look at baby and grown animals together.
skills.teach: Baby animals look like their parents! Find each animal's baby.

skills.subject: science
skills.title: Alive or Not?
skills.activity: Living things grow, eat, and move! Tap what's alive and what's not.
skills.parentTip: Characteristics of living things. Point out what's alive vs. an object on a walk.
skills.teach: Living things grow, eat, and move! Tap what's alive and what's not.

skills.subject: science
skills.title: Day or Night?
skills.activity: Owls and bats wake at night, bees buzz in the day. Tap when each animal is awake!
skills.parentTip: Day and night patterns in animal behavior. Talk about which animals you see when.
skills.teach: Owls and bats wake at night, bees buzz in the day. Tap when each animal is awake!

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Make 5
skills.activity: Some animals are here! Tap how many more make 5.
skills.parentTip: Making 5 from two parts. Use fingers or beans to show 3 and 2 make 5.
skills.teach: Some animals are here! Tap how many more make 5.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Which Has More?
skills.activity: Two groups of animals! Tap the group with more, or with fewer.
skills.parentTip: Comparing groups. Line up two sets of objects and compare which has more.
skills.teach: Two groups of animals! Tap the group with more, or with fewer.

skills.subject: science
skills.title: Egg or Not?
skills.activity: Which animals hatch from eggs? Tap the egg-layers and the ones born live.
skills.parentTip: How animals have young. Hens lay eggs; puppies are born live.
skills.teach: Which animals hatch from eggs? Tap the egg-layers and the ones born live.

skills.subject: science
skills.title: Wild or Pet?
skills.activity: Pets live with us, wild animals live on their own. Tap which is which!
skills.parentTip: Classifying animals. Talk about your pets vs. animals at the zoo.
skills.teach: Pets live with us, wild animals live on their own. Tap which is which!

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Bigger or Smaller?
skills.activity: Compare two things! Which is bigger, taller, or heavier? Which is smaller, shorter, or lighter?
skills.parentTip: Comparing size, height, and weight. Compare real objects around the house together.
skills.teach: Compare two things! Which is bigger, taller, or heavier? Which is smaller, shorter, or lighter?

skills.subject: math
skills.title: What Comes Next?
skills.activity: Look at the color pattern and tap what comes next! Red, blue, red, blue...
skills.parentTip: Recognizing and extending patterns. Try clap-stomp body patterns together too.
skills.teach: Look at the color pattern and tap what comes next! Red, blue, red, blue...

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Flat or Solid?
skills.activity: Some shapes are flat like a circle, some are solid like a ball. Tell which is which!
skills.parentTip: Flat (2D) vs solid (3D) shapes. Hold a ball, a box, and a can while you play.
skills.teach: Some shapes are flat like a circle, some are solid like a ball. Tell which is which!

skills.subject: science
skills.title: Plant or Animal?
skills.activity: Sort living things! Which is a plant, which is an animal, which can fly, which lives in water?
skills.parentTip: Sorting plants and animals by observable characteristics. Spot living things together on a walk.
skills.teach: Sort living things! Which is a plant, which is an animal, which can fly, which lives in water?

skills.subject: reading
skills.title: Rhyme Time
skills.activity: Find the word that rhymes! Cat and hat, dog and frog. Say them out loud!
skills.parentTip: Rhyming is a key reading sound skill. Say the words aloud together to hear the rhyme.
skills.teach: Find the word that rhymes! Cat and hat, dog and frog. Say them out loud!

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Number Detective
skills.activity: Count the dots and find the number, or read the number and find the group that shows it!
skills.parentTip: Connecting numbers to how many. He counts a group and matches it to the numeral, both directions.
skills.teach: Count the dots and find the number, or read the number and find the group that shows it!

skills.subject: reading
skills.title: Capital Letter Detective
skills.activity: Capital letters are the big ones. Spot the capitals hiding in each row!
skills.parentTip: Big letters start sentences and names. Let him say each one aloud.
skills.teach: Capital letters are the big ones. Spot the capitals hiding in each row!

skills.subject: reading
skills.title: Match the Letter Buddies
skills.activity: Every big letter has a little buddy. Tap a letter, then tap its partner!
skills.parentTip: Matching big to small builds letter recognition both ways.

lesson.prompt: Match the big letter to its little buddy.

skills.teach: Every big letter has a little buddy. Tap a letter, then tap its partner!

skills.subject: reading
skills.title: Letter Sounds Safari
skills.activity: Letters make sounds. Hunt for the word that starts with the same sound!
skills.parentTip: Say the sound, not the letter name: /k/, not 'see'.
skills.teach: Every letter makes a sound. A says 'ah', B says 'buh'. Match the letter to its sound.

skills.subject: reading
skills.title: Barnyard Rhyme Time
skills.activity: Rhyming words sound alike at the end. Tap the one that rhymes!
skills.parentTip: Say the words out loud together so he hears the rhyme.
skills.teach: Rhyming words sound alike at the end. Tap the one that rhymes!

skills.subject: reading
skills.title: Sound It Out
skills.activity: Stretch the sounds, then snap them together into a word!
skills.parentTip: Robot-talk the sounds slowly, then blend fast.
skills.teach: To read a word, blend the sounds together: c-a-t makes 'cat'. Slide the sounds into one word.

skills.subject: reading
skills.title: Star Words
skills.activity: Read the little sentence and pick the star word that fits!
skills.parentTip: Star words (see, go, is, like, and…) show up in every sentence. He reads the whole sentence and picks the word that makes sense — reading, not just matching. Read it aloud together with each choice if he's stuck.
skills.teach: Star words like see, go, is, like, and 'and' pop up in every sentence. Read the whole sentence and pick the word that makes it make sense.

skills.subject: reading
skills.title: What Happens First?
skills.activity: Stories happen in order. Put the day in the right order!
skills.parentTip: Sequencing a familiar routine builds story retelling.

lesson.prompt: Put the day in order, first to last.

skills.teach: Stories happen in order. Think about what happened FIRST, then next, then last.

skills.subject: reading
skills.title: How Books Work
skills.activity: Books have a secret map. Show that you know which way the words go!
skills.parentTip: These print rules make reading click.

questions.prompt: Which way do the words go?
When a line ends, go to the...

skills.teach: A book has a front cover, and we read the words from left to right, top to bottom.

skills.subject: reading
skills.title: Letter Detective
skills.activity: Find letters by their name or the sound they make. Big and little letters with a sound and a word for each!
skills.parentTip: Letter recognition and letter sounds. Say the sound, not the name: /b/, not 'bee'.
skills.teach: Find letters by their name or the sound they make. Big and little letters with a sound and a word for each!

skills.subject: writing
skills.title: Write Your Name
skills.activity: Trace each letter of your name with your finger!
skills.parentTip: Tracing the letters of his name with a finger is real early handwriting.
skills.teach: Your name is special! Follow the dots with your finger to trace each letter of your name.

skills.subject: writing
skills.title: Trace Capital Letters
skills.activity: Trace each big capital letter with your finger!
skills.parentTip: Forming capital letters by tracing builds handwriting control.
skills.teach: Capital letters are the BIG letters. Follow the dots with your finger to trace each one.

skills.subject: writing
skills.title: Label the Animal
skills.activity: Labeling is writing the first letter. Trace the starting letter of each animal!
skills.parentTip: Hearing the first sound and writing its letter is early labeling/writing.
skills.teach: To label something, you write its first letter. Say the animal, hear the first sound, then trace that letter.

skills.subject: writing
skills.title: Write 1 to 5!
skills.activity: Write the numbers! Trace each one with your finger.
skills.parentTip: He's great with numbers — now he writes them. Say the number as he traces it.
skills.teach: Write the numbers! Trace each one with your finger.

skills.subject: writing
skills.title: Write 6 to 10!
skills.activity: Write the bigger numbers! Trace each one with your finger.
skills.parentTip: Writing numbers cements what he already counts. Zero is a nice round loop.
skills.teach: Write the bigger numbers! Trace each one with your finger.

skills.subject: writing
skills.title: Letters G to L
skills.activity: More capital letters! Trace each one with your finger.
skills.parentTip: A few letters at a time. Trace slowly; neatness comes with practice.
skills.teach: More capital letters! Trace each one with your finger.

skills.subject: writing
skills.title: Letters M to R
skills.activity: Keep going through the alphabet! Trace each letter.
skills.parentTip: He's building the whole alphabet now. Cheer each finished letter.
skills.teach: Keep going through the alphabet! Trace each letter.

skills.subject: writing
skills.title: Letters S to Z
skills.activity: The last letters of the alphabet! Trace each one.
skills.parentTip: Finishing the alphabet is a big deal — make it a celebration.
skills.teach: The last letters of the alphabet! Trace each one.

skills.subject: writing
skills.title: Write Mama's Name
skills.activity: Write a name you love! Trace each letter of PAIGE.
skills.parentTip: Writing a family name is meaningful practice. Say each letter with him: P-A-I-G-E.
skills.teach: Write a name you love! Trace each letter of PAIGE.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Count the Critters
skills.activity: Count the animals, then type how many!
skills.parentTip: He has to actually count and type the number — no guessing from choices.
skills.teach: Counting means saying one number for each thing. Point to each animal: 1, 2, 3... The last number is how many!

skills.subject: math
skills.title: How Many in All?
skills.activity: Put both groups together, count them ALL, and type it!
skills.parentTip: Adding as 'put together and count all,' then producing the number.
skills.teach: To add, put both groups together and count them ALL. 2 chicks and 2 more chicks — count all of them: 4!

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Count by 2s
skills.activity: Count the pairs 2 at a time, then type how many!
skills.parentTip: Real pairs make the 'skip' visible; typing the total can't be guessed.
skills.teach: Things come in pairs — 2 at a time, like shoes. Count the pairs: 2, 4, 6. That's counting by 2s!

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Count by 5s
skills.activity: Each hand is 5 fingers. Count by 5s and type it!
skills.parentTip: Hands give him a built-in group of 5; he skip-counts and types the total.
skills.teach: One hand has 5 fingers. Count hands by 5s: 5, 10, 15. Each new hand adds 5 more!

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Count to 20
skills.activity: Tap each animal and count out loud all the way to 20!
skills.parentTip: Counting things he can see keeps it concrete.

lesson.prompt: Tap each paw and count to 20!

skills.teach: Tap each animal and count out loud all the way to 20!

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Count by Tens
skills.activity: Big numbers zoom by tens. Put them in order!
skills.parentTip: Clap on each ten to add rhythm.
skills.teach: Big numbers zoom by tens. Put them in order!

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Count the Eggs
skills.activity: Touch one egg for each number. Count carefully to 10!
skills.parentTip: One tap per number builds one-to-one counting.

lesson.prompt: Tap each egg as you count to 10!

skills.teach: Touch one egg for each number. Count carefully to 10!

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Number Order 0-10
skills.activity: Numbers have an order too. Line them up from 0 to 10!
skills.parentTip: Recognizing order supports writing the numbers.
skills.teach: Numbers have an order too. Line them up from 0 to 10!

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Who Has More?
skills.activity: What comes next when we count? Which number is more or less? Tap it!
skills.parentTip: Connect to snacks: 'who has more?' and count up together.
skills.teach: What comes next when we count? Which number is more or less? Tap it!

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Adding On
skills.activity: Put groups together to make more. Solve each one!
skills.parentTip: Let him use fingers or beans to check.
skills.teach: Put groups together to make more. Solve each one!

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Taking Away
skills.activity: Some go away, and you find what's left. Solve each one!
skills.parentTip: Act it out with carrots and a hungry bunny.
skills.teach: Some go away, and you find what's left. Solve each one!

skills.subject: math
skills.title: 2D Shape Hunt
skills.activity: Flat shapes have names. Tap the right one!
skills.parentTip: Spot these shapes together on a walk.
skills.teach: Flat shapes have names. Tap the right one!

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Solid Shapes
skills.activity: Some shapes you can hold. Match the object to its shape!
skills.parentTip: Hold a ball, a box, and a can while you play.

questions.prompt: A ball is shaped like a...
A box is shaped like a...
A can is shaped like a...

skills.teach: Some shapes you can hold. Match the object to its shape!

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Which One Is Different?
skills.activity: Sorting means things that belong together. Tap the odd one out!
skills.parentTip: Ask him to explain why it doesn't belong.
skills.teach: Sorting means things that belong together. Tap the odd one out!

skills.subject: math
skills.title: What Comes Next?
skills.activity: Patterns repeat. Find what comes next in the pattern!
skills.parentTip: Try clap-stomp body patterns too.
skills.teach: Patterns repeat. Find what comes next in the pattern!

skills.subject: science
skills.title: Weather Watcher
skills.activity: Be the weather reporter. Match the weather to what you'd do!
skills.parentTip: Look out the window together first.
skills.teach: Be the weather reporter. Match the weather to what you'd do!

skills.subject: science
skills.title: What They Need
skills.activity: Plants and animals need food, water, and sunlight. Tap what each one needs!
skills.parentTip: Walk to your plants and animals and talk about what they need.
skills.teach: Plants and animals need food, water, and sunlight. Tap what each one needs!

skills.subject: science
skills.title: Push or Pull?
skills.activity: Things move when we push or pull. Tap how each one moves!
skills.parentTip: Try it together with a cart, a door, and a wagon afterward.
skills.teach: Things move when we push or pull. Tap how each one moves!

skills.subject: science
skills.title: Weather Watch
skills.activity: Look at the weather and name it: sunny, rainy, cloudy, snowy, windy, or stormy. Find it by name or by what it does!
skills.parentTip: Observing and describing weather. Look out the window together and name today's weather.
skills.teach: Look at the weather and name it: sunny, rainy, cloudy, snowy, windy, or stormy. Find it by name or by what it does!

skills.subject: life
skills.title: American Symbols
skills.activity: Find the U.S. flag, the Statue of Liberty, the bald eagle, and more! Learn what each one means.
skills.parentTip: Identifying national symbols. Point them out on money, at school, and around town.
skills.teach: Find the U.S. flag, the Statue of Liberty, the bald eagle, and more! Learn what each one means.

skills.subject: life
skills.title: Community Helpers
skills.activity: Who puts out fires? Who helps you learn? Find the community helpers and what they do!
skills.parentTip: Identifying helpers in school and the community. Talk about helpers you meet in daily life.
skills.teach: Who puts out fires? Who helps you learn? Find the community helpers and what they do!

skills.subject: life
skills.title: Party on the Farm!
skills.activity: What does Thanksgiving celebrate? What about MLK Day? Match each holiday to what it means!
skills.parentTip: Knowing what major holidays celebrate. Connect each to your own family traditions.
skills.teach: What does Thanksgiving celebrate? What about MLK Day? Match each holiday to what it means!

skills.subject: life
skills.title: My Family
skills.activity: Meet your family and what everyone does at home! Two moms, Mommy and Maddy, plus all the cats and dogs.
skills.parentTip: Naming family members and their roles. Families come in all kinds; this one celebrates yours.
skills.teach: Meet your family and what everyone does at home! Two moms, Mommy and Maddy, plus all the cats and dogs.

skills.subject: life
skills.title: Name Your Feelings
skills.activity: Drag each face to the feeling it shows. A new mix of feelings every time!
skills.parentTip: No pressure to feel any of these, just to name them. Talk about times he's felt each one.
skills.teach: Drag each face to the feeling it shows. A new mix of feelings every time!

skills.subject: life
skills.title: Days of the Week
skills.activity: The week repeats in order. Put the days in order!
skills.parentTip: A days-of-the-week song helps the order stick.
skills.teach: The week has 7 days in order: Sunday, Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, Saturday.

skills.subject: life
skills.title: Farm Helpers
skills.activity: Good helpers make the farm run. Tap the helpful choice!
skills.parentTip: Talk about real jobs he could pick afterward, his choice.
skills.teach: Being a helper means doing kind things, like cleaning up or helping a friend. Helpers make everyone happy.

skills.subject: reading
skills.title: Short and Long Vowels
skills.activity: Long vowels say their name. Tap the word with the long vowel sound!
skills.parentTip: Stretch the vowel: cake says a long A, cat says short a.
skills.teach: Long vowels say their own name, like the A in CAKE. Short vowels are quick, like the a in CAT. Listen for the name!

skills.subject: reading
skills.title: Team Sounds (sh, ch, th)
skills.activity: Two letters, one sound. Tap the word that starts with the team sound!
skills.parentTip: sh, ch, th each make one sound from two letters.
skills.teach: Some letters team up to make ONE sound: SH says shhh, CH says choo-choo, TH says this. Two letters, one sound.

skills.subject: reading
skills.title: Word-Wall Words
skills.activity: Tricky words you just have to know. Tap the right spelling!
skills.parentTip: A few each day beats all of them at once.
skills.teach: Some words we just KNOW by sight, like 'said' and 'the'. You don't sound them out, you just remember them.

skills.subject: reading
skills.title: Read and Answer
skills.activity: Read each little sentence, then tap the answer!
skills.parentTip: Reading for meaning is the goal. Read it together if he likes.

questions.prompt: 'The hen is red.'  What color is the hen?
'A pig can run.'  Can the pig run?
'I see two cows.'  How many cows?

skills.teach: Good readers stop and think. Read the sentence, then answer what happened in it.

skills.subject: reading
skills.title: Question Words
skills.activity: Good readers ask questions. Match the question word to what it asks!
skills.parentTip: Who/what/where/when help him think about a story.

lesson.prompt: Match the question word to what it asks about.

skills.teach: Asking words: WHO is a person, WHERE is a place, WHEN is a time, WHY is a reason.

skills.subject: reading
skills.title: Main Idea
skills.activity: The main idea is what it's mostly about. Tap the best main idea!
skills.parentTip: Prompt: 'In one breath, what was it about?'

questions.prompt: A book about feeding, brushing, and walking a dog is mostly about...
A book about seeds, sun, and water growing a plant is mostly about...

skills.teach: The main idea is what the story is MOSTLY about. Ask yourself: what's the big thing here?

skills.subject: reading
skills.title: Blends
skills.activity: Blends keep both sounds. Tap the word that starts with the blend!
skills.parentTip: Unlike team sounds, you hear both letters in a blend.
skills.teach: In a blend you hear each letter, but they slide together fast, like S+T in STOP or B+L in BLUE.

skills.subject: writing
skills.title: Build a Sentence
skills.activity: Tap the words in order to build a sentence that makes sense!
skills.parentTip: It starts with a capital and ends with a period. Point that out.

lesson.prompt: Tap the words in order to make a sentence.

skills.teach: A sentence has a naming part (who) and an action part (does what). It starts with a capital and ends with a period.

skills.subject: writing
skills.title: Spot the Opinion
skills.activity: An opinion tells what YOU think. Tap the opinion sentence!
skills.parentTip: A fact can be checked; an opinion is a feeling or favorite.

questions.correct: Summer is the most fun season.

skills.teach: A FACT is true for everyone. An OPINION is what someone feels, like 'I think ice cream is best'.

skills.subject: writing
skills.title: Put the Story in Order
skills.activity: A story happens in order. Tap the parts first to last!
skills.parentTip: Sequencing words: first, then, next, last.

lesson.prompt: Tap the story parts in order.

skills.teach: Stories go in order: first, next, then, last. Put the parts in the order they happened.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Count to 120
skills.activity: Numbers keep going past 100. Tap what comes next!
skills.parentTip: Starting mid-count is the real skill.
skills.teach: Numbers keep going past 100! After 119 comes 120. Keep counting up and don't stop at 100.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Add Within 20
skills.activity: Add the numbers and type your answer!
skills.parentTip: Any strategy that gets there is a good one.
skills.teach: Adding puts groups together to get MORE. 8 + 5 means start at 8 and count up 5 more.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Subtract Within 20
skills.activity: Take away and type what's left!
skills.parentTip: Counting up or counting back both work.
skills.teach: Subtracting means taking AWAY. 14 − 6 means start at 14 and count back 6.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Story Problems
skills.activity: See the story: some come, some go away. Tap how many!
skills.parentTip: He solves it by looking, not reading. Add and subtract within 20.
skills.teach: Word problems tell a little story with numbers. Read it, find the numbers, then decide to add or take away.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Tens and Ones
skills.activity: Numbers are made of tens and ones. Solve each one!
skills.parentTip: Bundles of ten straws make this real.
skills.teach: A two-digit number has tens and ones. In 34, the 3 means 3 tens (30) and the 4 means 4 ones.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Compare Numbers
skills.activity: Which number is bigger? Tap the right one!
skills.parentTip: The 'alligator mouth' eats the bigger number.
skills.teach: The > sign is like a hungry mouth that eats the BIGGER number. 54 > 45.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Measure with Paperclips
skills.activity: Measure by lining up units with no gaps. Solve the measuring puzzle!
skills.parentTip: No gaps and no overlaps is the key rule.

problems.prompt: How long is the pencil? Count the clips!
A carrot is 4 clips, a worm is 1 clip. How many longer is the carrot?

skills.teach: To measure length, line up units end to end, like paperclips, and count how many fit.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Tell Time
skills.activity: Read the clock to the hour and half hour. Tap the time!
skills.parentTip: The short hand is the hour, the long hand is minutes.

questions.prompt: Short hand on 3, long hand on 12

skills.teach: On a clock the SHORT hand shows the hour, the LONG hand shows minutes. Long hand on 12 means o'clock!

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Tally and Count
skills.activity: Tally marks count in groups. Solve the counting puzzle!
skills.parentTip: Four lines and a slash makes a group of five.

problems.prompt: A group of tally marks (a 5) plus 2 more = ?
6 dogs, 2 run away. How many left?

skills.teach: Tally marks count by ones: one line for each thing. The 5th mark crosses the group so you can count by 5s.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Halves and Fourths
skills.activity: Equal parts have fancy names. Tap the right one!
skills.parentTip: Sharing a snack equally makes this real.

questions.prompt: Which is BIGGER, one half or one fourth?

skills.teach: Halves are 2 EQUAL parts. Fourths are 4 EQUAL parts. Equal means all the same size.

skills.subject: science
skills.title: Light and Sound
skills.activity: Sound comes from vibrations, shadows come from light. Tap what's true!
skills.parentTip: Let him feel his throat hum to feel a vibration.

questions.prompt: A shadow is made when something blocks...
Pluck a rubber band. It makes sound because it...

skills.teach: We need LIGHT to see. SOUND happens when something shakes, or vibrates, like a drum or a guitar string.

skills.subject: science
skills.title: Plant and Animal Parts
skills.activity: Body parts have jobs. Match the part to what it does!
skills.parentTip: Walk the farm and let him be the tour guide after.

lesson.prompt: Match the part to its job.

skills.teach: Every part has a job! Roots drink water, leaves catch sunlight, wings help birds fly, ears help us hear.

skills.subject: science
skills.title: Sky Patterns
skills.activity: The sky changes in patterns. Tap what's true about the sky!
skills.parentTip: A few nights of moon drawings show the pattern.

questions.prompt: In the morning, the sun is in the...
At night we usually see the...
The sun seems to move across the sky during the...

skills.teach: The sun rises in the morning and sets at night. The moon and stars come out at night. It repeats every day.

skills.subject: life
skills.title: Today's Date
skills.activity: A date has a month, day, and year. Put a date in order!
skills.parentTip: A wall calendar he can point to helps.

lesson.prompt: Put a date in the right order.

skills.teach: A date has a day, a month, and a year. A calendar helps us find what day today is.

skills.subject: life
skills.title: Know Your Coins
skills.activity: Coins are worth different amounts. Match each coin to its value!
skills.parentTip: Real coins to hold make the values stick.

lesson.prompt: Match the coin to how much it's worth.

skills.teach: A penny is 1¢, a nickel is 5¢, a dime is 10¢, a quarter is 25¢. Coins are worth different amounts.

skills.subject: life
skills.title: Calm-Down Game
skills.activity: Big feelings need calm tools. Tap the healthy choice!
skills.parentTip: Knowing the tools when calm makes them easier to use later.

questions.prompt: A good way to calm down is...
If you feel mad, you can...

skills.teach: When big feelings come, we can pause and breathe slow. Breathe in like smelling a flower, out like blowing a candle.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Big Apple Add-Up
skills.activity: Bigger groups now! Put them together and count them all.
skills.parentTip: Same idea as Add to 5, just larger. Counting on from the bigger group is the next step.
skills.teach: Bigger groups now! Put them together and count them all.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Ten Fish, Some Swim Off
skills.activity: Bigger numbers. Some go away — count what's left!
skills.parentTip: Start from 10 and count back. Fingers help: put some down, count what's up.
skills.teach: Bigger numbers. Some go away — count what's left!

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Which Number Hid?
skills.activity: Numbers go in order. Tap the one that's missing!
skills.parentTip: Count out loud together to hear which number was skipped.
skills.teach: Numbers go in order. Tap the one that's missing!

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Twin Bunnies
skills.activity: Two groups the SAME size. Count them all!
skills.parentTip: Doubles are easy to remember and make bigger adding faster: 4 and 4 is 8.
skills.teach: Two groups the SAME size. Count them all!

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Fill the Nest
skills.activity: The nest holds 10 eggs. Count the EMPTY spots to fill it!
skills.parentTip: Ten spots, some have a chick. He counts the empty boxes — the amount needed to make ten. Concrete counting, no mental math.
skills.teach: The nest holds 10 eggs. Count the EMPTY spots to fill it!

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Three Little Groups
skills.activity: Three little groups. Put them together and count all!
skills.parentTip: Adding three numbers is a first-grade step. Count every object, group by group.
skills.teach: Three little groups. Put them together and count all!

skills.subject: reading
skills.title: Read Along with Leo
skills.activity: Read the little sentence, then answer about it!
skills.parentTip: He reads one short sentence and answers who or what. That's real comprehension.

questions.prompt: The cat is big. Who is big?
A dog can run. What can run?
The sun is hot. What is hot?
I see a red bug. What color is it?

skills.teach: Read the little sentence, then answer about it!

skills.subject: reading
skills.title: Finish the Story
skills.activity: Pick the word that makes the sentence make sense!
skills.parentTip: Read the whole sentence with each choice and hear which one sounds right.
skills.teach: Pick the word that makes the sentence make sense!

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Add to 5
skills.activity: Put the two groups together and count them ALL!
skills.parentTip: Point to every object and count from one — that's what adding is.
skills.teach: Put the two groups together and count them ALL!

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Take Away to 5
skills.activity: Some go away. Count the ones that are LEFT!
skills.parentTip: Use snacks: start with a few, eat one, count what's left. That's subtracting.
skills.teach: Some go away. Count the ones that are LEFT!

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Teen Numbers
skills.activity: A teen number is 10 and some more. Count them all!
skills.parentTip: Ten and 3 more is 13. Seeing the ten first makes the big numbers easy.
skills.teach: A teen number is 10 and some more. Count them all!

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Count to 10
skills.activity: Point to each one and count. How many in all?
skills.parentTip: Touch one object per number word, all the way to ten.
skills.teach: Point to each one and count. How many in all?

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Animal Add-Up!
skills.activity: More animals come! Put them together and count them all.
skills.parentTip: Act it out with his toy animals: a few here, a few more, count them all.
skills.teach: More animals come! Put them together and count them all.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Ducks Swim Away!
skills.activity: Some animals leave! Count the ones that are LEFT.
skills.parentTip: Line up his animals, walk a few away, count who stays.
skills.teach: Some animals leave! Count the ones that are LEFT.

skills.subject: reading
skills.title: Blend It
skills.activity: Say each sound, then push them together into a word!
skills.parentTip: Stretch it slow — c...a...t — then fast: cat! That's blending.
skills.teach: Say each sound, then push them together into a word!

skills.subject: reading
skills.title: Beginning Sounds
skills.activity: Every word starts with a sound. Tap the letter it starts with!
skills.parentTip: Say the word slowly and stretch the first sound: mmmoon starts with m.
skills.teach: Every word starts with a sound. Tap the letter it starts with!

skills.subject: reading
skills.title: Rhyme Time
skills.activity: Rhyming words end the same. Tap the one that rhymes!
skills.parentTip: Cat, hat, bat all end in -at. Make silly rhymes together.
skills.teach: Rhyming words end the same. Tap the one that rhymes!

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Tap and Count to 3
skills.activity: Point and count each one: 1, 2, 3. Tap all 3 chicks!
skills.parentTip: Touch one object per number word — that one-to-one touch is the whole skill.
skills.teach: Point and count each one: 1, 2, 3. Tap all 3 chicks!

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Tap and Count to 5
skills.activity: Count each star as you tap it: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5!
skills.parentTip: Counting on fingers or real toys makes this stick.
skills.teach: Count each star as you tap it: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5!

skills.subject: math
skills.title: How Many Chicks?
skills.activity: Count the animals, then tap the number that says how many.
skills.parentTip: The LAST number he counts is the answer — that's cardinality.
skills.teach: Count the animals, then tap the number that says how many.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Bigger or Smaller
skills.activity: One is big, one is little. Tap the BIGGER one!
skills.parentTip: Compare real things around the house — the bigger cup, the smaller spoon.
skills.teach: One is big, one is little. Tap the BIGGER one!

skills.subject: math
skills.title: What Comes Next?
skills.activity: Patterns repeat! See the pattern, then tap what comes next.
skills.parentTip: Make patterns with blocks or snacks: red, blue, red, blue...
skills.teach: Patterns repeat! See the pattern, then tap what comes next.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Find the Shape
skills.activity: Shapes have names. Tap the one that matches!
skills.parentTip: Hunt for circles and squares around the house together.
skills.teach: Shapes have names. Tap the one that matches!

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Colors
skills.activity: Each color has a name. Tap the right color!
skills.parentTip: Name colors of his toys and clothes through the day.
skills.teach: Each color has a name. Tap the right color!

skills.subject: reading
skills.title: Big and Little Letters
skills.activity: Every BIG letter has a little partner. Match them up!
skills.parentTip: B and b are partners, A and a are partners. Spot pairs on signs together.

lesson.prompt: Match the big letter to its little partner.

skills.teach: Every BIG letter has a little partner. Match them up!

skills.subject: reading
skills.title: First Sounds
skills.activity: Every word starts with a sound. Tap the first letter!
skills.parentTip: Say the word slowly and stretch the first sound: mmmoon.
skills.teach: Every word starts with a sound. Tap the first letter!

skills.subject: reading
skills.title: Rhyme Time
skills.activity: Rhyming words sound the same at the end. Tap the one that rhymes!
skills.parentTip: Sing rhyming songs — the ear for rhyme comes before reading.
skills.teach: Rhyming words sound the same at the end. Tap the one that rhymes!

skills.subject: science
skills.title: Which Animal?
skills.activity: You know your animals! Tap the one it asks for.
skills.parentTip: Let him be the expert — he can name more than you'd think.
skills.teach: You know your animals! Tap the one it asks for.

skills.subject: science
skills.title: Where Do They Live?
skills.activity: Every animal has a home. Match each animal to where it lives!
skills.parentTip: Talk about where your farm animals sleep and live.

lesson.prompt: Match the animal to its home.

skills.teach: Every animal has a home. Match each animal to where it lives!

skills.subject: science
skills.title: Baby Animals
skills.activity: Baby animals have special names. Tap the right one!
skills.parentTip: A puppy, a kitten, a calf, a chick — name the babies on the farm.
skills.teach: Baby animals have special names. Tap the right one!

skills.subject: life
skills.title: Happy or Sad?
skills.activity: Faces show feelings. Just two faces — tap the feeling!
skills.parentTip: Reading faces is hard for him, so this keeps it to two very different faces and one clear feeling. Make the face yourself as you name it: big smile for happy, frown for sad.
skills.teach: Faces show feelings. Just two faces — tap the feeling!

skills.subject: math
skills.title: One More Hops In
skills.activity: One more hops in! Count them all and type how many.
skills.parentTip: One more is just the next counting number. 6, then one more is 7. Count up by one.
skills.teach: One MORE means the very next number. 6 and one more is 7. Count them all and type how many.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: One Hops Away
skills.activity: One goes away. Count what's LEFT and type it.
skills.parentTip: One less is the number right before it. 7, one less is 6. Count back by one.
skills.teach: One LESS means the number right before. 7 and one goes away leaves 6. Count what's left.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Double the Herd
skills.activity: Two groups the SAME size. Count them all!
skills.parentTip: Doubles are the easiest facts to memorize and they make bigger adding fast: 7 and 7 is 14.
skills.teach: Doubles are two groups the SAME size. 7 and 7 is 14. Learn these and big adding gets easy!

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Ten and Some More
skills.activity: A teen number is a full ten and some more. Count them all!
skills.parentTip: See the ten first, then count on the extras: ten and 4 more is 14. This is how teen numbers work.
skills.teach: A teen number is a full ten and some more. See the ten, then count on the extras: ten and 4 is 14.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Count On, Cowboy!
skills.activity: Start big, then count up a few more. Where do you land?
skills.parentTip: Instead of counting from one, start at the big number and count on: start at 12, count 13, 14, 15. Faster and first-grade smart.
skills.teach: Counting on is a smart shortcut: start at the BIG number and count up the little one. Start at 12, count 13, 14, 15.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Fill the Ten
skills.activity: The tank holds 10 fish. Count the empty ⬜ spots to fill it!
skills.parentTip: Ten spots, some already have a fish. He counts the empty boxes — that's how many MORE make ten. Concrete, no mental math.
skills.teach: To make ten, fill every spot. Count the EMPTY boxes — that's how many more you need to reach ten.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Big Barn Add-Up
skills.activity: Bigger groups that cross ten. Put them together and count all!
skills.parentTip: Same as Add to 10, just past ten now. He can make a ten first, or just count them all.
skills.teach: Adding past ten works the same way: put both groups together and count them all, right across ten.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Big Take-Away
skills.activity: Bigger numbers now. Some go away — count what's left!
skills.parentTip: Start at the big number and count back, or count up from the small one. Either way works.
skills.teach: Taking away from a bigger number: start at the number and count back, or count up from the smaller one.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Ten More, Ten Less
skills.activity: Ten more or ten less just changes the tens. Type the new number!
skills.parentTip: Ten more than 25 is 35 — only the tens digit goes up by one. Ten less goes down by one ten.
skills.teach: Ten more or ten less only changes the TENS. Ten more than 25 is 35. Ten less than 30 is 20.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Count by Tens
skills.activity: Count by tens: 10, 20, 30… Type the next number!
skills.parentTip: Counting by tens is the fast way to count big groups. Only the tens digit changes.
skills.teach: Counting by tens jumps ten each time: 10, 20, 30, 40. Only the first digit changes.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Count by Fives
skills.activity: Count by fives: 5, 10, 15… Type the next number!
skills.parentTip: Counting by fives is like counting hands. Great for telling time later.
skills.teach: Counting by fives goes 5, 10, 15, 20 — like counting fingers on each hand.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Count by Twos
skills.activity: Count by twos: 2, 4, 6… Type the next number!
skills.parentTip: Counting by twos skips every other number. Count socks or shoes in twos.
skills.teach: Counting by twos skips every other number: 2, 4, 6, 8. Count in pairs.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Doubles Plus One
skills.activity: Almost a double! Do the double, then add one more.
skills.parentTip: 6 + 7 is just 6 + 6 and one more. Knowing doubles makes these easy.
skills.teach: A near-double is a double plus one. 6 + 7 is 6 + 6 (that's 12) and one more makes 13.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Tens and Ones
skills.activity: A whole ten (or two!) and some more. Type how many in all.
skills.parentTip: 20 and 3 more is 23. See the tens first, then count on the extra ones.
skills.teach: See the tens first, then add the ones. 20 and 3 more is 23. Two tens and three.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: How Many More?
skills.activity: Two groups. Count how many MORE the bigger group has!
skills.parentTip: Line them up and see the extra. Comparing is a kind of subtracting.
skills.teach: To find how many MORE, match them up and count the extras the bigger group has.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Barn Story
skills.activity: A little story on the farm. Read it, then type the answer!
skills.parentTip: Some come, some go. Act it out with his toy animals if he likes.

problems.prompt: 6 🐮 in the barn. 3 more come in. How many now?
10 🐔 pecking. 4 go outside. How many left?
5 🐑 here and 7 🐑 there. How many sheep?
8 🐷 by the trough. 2 run to the mud. How many left?

skills.teach: A story problem hides numbers in words. Find the numbers, then add if more come or take away if some go.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Pond Story
skills.activity: More animal stories! Read it, then type how many.
skills.parentTip: Pull out the numbers and decide: are we adding more, or taking some away?

problems.prompt: 9 🦆 on the pond. 5 fly away. How many left?
7 🐴 in the field and 6 more come. How many?
12 🐝 at the hive. 4 fly off. How many left?

skills.teach: Read the animal story, find the two numbers, and decide: are we putting together or taking away?

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Make a Ten!
skills.activity: Fill up to ten first, then add the rest. Type the total!
skills.parentTip: 9 + 3: give 1 to the 9 to make 10, then 2 more is 12. A big first-grade trick.
skills.teach: Make a ten first! For 9 + 3, move 1 over to make 10, then 2 more is 12. Tens are easy to add on.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Count On Past Ten
skills.activity: Start at the big number and count up a few more!
skills.parentTip: Don't start from one. Start at 16 and count 17, 18, 19.
skills.teach: Start at the big number and count on the small one: 16, then 17, 18, 19. No need to start at one.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: The Number Before
skills.activity: Which number comes right BEFORE? Type it!
skills.parentTip: The number before is one less. Before 13 is 12. Count backward one step.
skills.teach: The number before is one less — the one you say just before it when counting. Before 13 is 12.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Count the Pennies
skills.activity: Each penny is 1 cent. Count them and type the cents!
skills.parentTip: A penny is worth 1¢, so counting pennies is just counting. Real coins make it click.
skills.teach: A penny is worth 1 cent, so the number of pennies IS the number of cents. Count them up!

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Which Is More?
skills.activity: Which number is bigger (or smaller)? Tap it!
skills.parentTip: Bigger numbers are farther along when you count. 14 comes after 9, so it's more.
skills.teach: The bigger number is the one you reach later when counting. 14 is more than 9.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Turn-Around Trick
skills.activity: 8 + 3 or 3 + 8? Same answer! Flip it and see.
skills.parentTip: Adding in either order gives the same total. Every fact he knows is secretly two facts, so this halves what there is to learn.
skills.teach: Adding in either order gives the same answer. If you know 8 + 3, you already know 3 + 8.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Find the Missing Number
skills.activity: A number is hiding! Which one finishes it?
skills.parentTip: Ask how many more to get there. Counting up from the smaller number is the easiest way in, and it is the same move as make-a-ten.
skills.teach: Something is missing! Count up from the number you have to the number you want, and that jump is the answer.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Add Three Numbers
skills.activity: Three numbers at once! Add two, then the last one.
skills.parentTip: Look for a pair that makes ten first. 4 + 6 + 3 is much easier as 10 + 3, and spotting the pair is the real skill.
skills.teach: Three numbers: look for two that make ten first, add those, then add what is left.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Tens and Ones Add-Up
skills.activity: Bigger numbers, easy way. Add the ones, or jump by tens.
skills.parentTip: 23 + 5 only changes the ones. 40 + 30 only changes the tens. The other part stays exactly where it was.
skills.teach: Adding ones only changes the ones. Adding tens only changes the tens. The other part stays the same.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Think Adding!
skills.activity: Taking away? Think adding instead. Same puzzle, easier way.
skills.parentTip: 10 - 8 is really eight and how many more make ten. Turning subtraction into addition lets him use facts he already owns instead of counting backward.
skills.teach: Instead of counting backward, ask what plus this makes the big number. 12 - 9 is 9 and 3 more.

skills.subject: reading
skills.title: Read the Word
skills.activity: Read the word, then tap the picture it means!
skills.parentTip: Sound it out slowly, then tap what it means. Picture answers, so he truly reads the word.
skills.teach: Read the word by blending its sounds, then pick the picture it means. c-a-t is cat! 🐱

skills.subject: reading
skills.title: Read the Word 2
skills.activity: More words to read! Tap the picture it means.
skills.parentTip: Three-sound words like hen and fox. Stretch the sounds, then blend.
skills.teach: Stretch each sound and blend: h-e-n is hen. Then tap the picture that matches.

skills.subject: reading
skills.title: Word Families
skills.activity: Words in a family end the same. Tap the one that fits!
skills.parentTip: The -ig family: pig, wig, dig. Same ending, just a new first sound.

questions.prompt: Which word is in the  -ig  family?
Which word is in the  -op  family?
Which word is in the  -ed  family?
Which word is in the  -un  family?

skills.teach: Words in a family share an ending, like -ig: pig, wig, dig. Find the one that ends the same.

skills.subject: reading
skills.title: Blends
skills.activity: Two letters slide together at the start. Tap the picture!
skills.parentTip: In a blend you hear both letters fast: st in star, fr in frog, sn in snake.
skills.teach: A blend slides two sounds together: st in star, fr in frog. You hear both letters, fast.

skills.subject: reading
skills.title: Team Sounds
skills.activity: Two letters make ONE sound. Tap the picture!
skills.parentTip: sh, ch, and th each make one sound from two letters: ship, chick, thumb.
skills.teach: Team sounds make ONE sound from two letters: sh in ship, ch in chick, th in thumb.

skills.subject: reading
skills.title: Finish the Sentence
skills.activity: Pick the word that makes the sentence make sense!
skills.parentTip: Read the whole sentence with each choice and hear which one sounds right.
skills.teach: Read the whole sentence and pick the word that makes sense. A fish can swim, not jump.

skills.subject: reading
skills.title: Yes or No?
skills.activity: Read the little sentence, then answer yes or no!
skills.parentTip: He reads for meaning and answers yes or no — no word to copy, so he has to understand it.

questions.prompt: The 🐶 runs fast.  Can the dog run?
The 🐱 is asleep.  Is the cat awake?
The 🐮 eats grass.  Does the cow eat grass?
The 🐟 can swim.  Can the fish fly?

skills.teach: Read the little sentence carefully, then decide yes or no. You have to understand it, not just match a word.

skills.subject: science
skills.title: Alive or Not?
skills.activity: Living things grow and eat. Tap the one that is ALIVE!
skills.parentTip: Living things need food, water, and air and can grow. Rocks and toys do not.
skills.teach: Living things eat, grow, and need water and air — like animals and plants. Rocks and toys do not.

skills.subject: science
skills.title: Animal Teams
skills.activity: Animals come in groups. Tap the group it belongs to!
skills.parentTip: Mammals have fur, birds have feathers, fish have fins, bugs have six legs.

questions.prompt: A 🐟 that swims with fins is a...

skills.teach: Animals come in groups: mammals have fur, birds have feathers, fish have fins, bugs have six legs.

skills.subject: science
skills.title: Who Eats What?
skills.activity: Every animal has a favorite food. Tap what it eats!
skills.parentTip: Rabbits love carrots, cows eat grass, bees drink from flowers. Talk about your farm animals.
skills.teach: Different animals eat different foods. Rabbits love carrots, cows eat grass, bees sip from flowers.

skills.subject: science
skills.title: Float or Sink?
skills.activity: Some things float, some sink. Tap what happens!
skills.parentTip: Try it in the bathtub! Heavy dense things sink, light things float.
skills.teach: Heavy, dense things sink; light things float. A rock sinks, a leaf floats. Try it in the tub!

skills.subject: life
skills.title: Push or Pull? 2
skills.activity: We move things by pushing or pulling. Tap which one!
skills.parentTip: A push moves something away, a pull brings it closer. Point them out around the house.

questions.prompt: To open a heavy door, you...
A dog on a leash, you...

skills.teach: A push moves something away from you; a pull brings it toward you. Doors, wagons, swings — push or pull.

skills.subject: writing
skills.title: Giraffe Neck Slide
skills.activity: Slide your finger down the giraffe's neck to the leaf. Top to bottom!
skills.parentTip: The top-to-bottom line is the first handwriting stroke. Starting at the top matters more than being straight.

steps.say: Warm up: slide down the giraffe's neck to the leaf!
l is a tall line down, like the giraffe's neck!
i is a short line down, then a dot on top!
t is a tall line down, then cross it!
Now write the whole word: lion!

skills.teach: Slide your finger down the giraffe's neck to the leaf. Top to bottom!

skills.subject: writing
skills.title: Worm Walk
skills.activity: Walk the worm across to the apple. Left to right, like reading!
skills.parentTip: Left-to-right lines are the second stroke, and the direction we read and write in.

steps.say: Warm up: walk the worm across to the apple!
e starts with a line across, then curls round!
f is a hook, a line down, then across!
t is a line down, then across!
Now write the whole word: hen!

skills.teach: Walk the worm across to the apple. Left to right, like reading!

skills.subject: writing
skills.title: Round the Nest
skills.activity: Walk the hen all the way around her nest. Start at the top and go left!
skills.parentTip: Starting a circle at the top and going left (counter-clockwise) is exactly how c, o, a, d and g begin.

steps.say: Warm up: walk the hen around her nest to the egg!
c curls left from the top, like the hen!
o curls all the way round!
a curls round, then a short line down!
Now write the whole word: cat!

skills.teach: Walk the hen all the way around her nest. Start at the top and go left!

skills.subject: writing
skills.title: Duck Pond Wave
skills.activity: Help the duck swim the waves across the pond!
skills.parentTip: Smooth up-and-down curves are the motion inside m, n, u and w. Slow and wavy beats fast and wobbly.

steps.say: Warm up: help the duck swim the waves to the lily pad!
u is a wave: down, curve, and up!
m is down, then two humps!
n is down, then one hump!
Now write the whole word: emu!

skills.teach: Help the duck swim the waves across the pond!

skills.subject: writing
skills.title: Fence Hop
skills.activity: The goat hops over every fence post to reach the hay!
skills.parentTip: Sharp up-and-down diagonals build v, w, z and the sides of A and M. Points, not curves.

steps.say: Warm up: the goat hops the fence posts to the hay!
v is slant down, slant up!
w is down, up, down, up!
z is across, slant down, across!
Now write the whole word: wolf!

skills.teach: The goat hops over every fence post to reach the hay!

skills.subject: writing
skills.title: Over the Barn
skills.activity: The bird flies up and over the barn in one big hump!
skills.parentTip: One smooth hump, left to right, is the top of h, m, n and r.

steps.say: Warm up: the bluebird flies up and over the barn to the tree!
h is a tall line, then a hump over!
r is a line down, then a little hook over!
b is a tall line, then a belly!
Now write the whole word: bear!

skills.teach: The bird flies up and over the barn in one big hump!

skills.subject: writing
skills.title: Bee Loops
skills.activity: The bee loops and loops on her way to the flower!
skills.parentTip: Loops are the hardest pre-writing shape and the start of e and l. It's fine if they overlap.

steps.say: Warm up: the bee loops her way to the flower!
e is a little loop: across, then curl round!
l loops up tall and back down!
b loops up, then round into a belly!
Now write the whole word: bee!

skills.teach: The bee loops and loops on her way to the flower!

skills.subject: writing
skills.title: Snail Spiral
skills.activity: Follow the snail round and round into the middle of his shell!
skills.parentTip: A spiral is a circle that keeps going. It builds the wrist control for small round letters.

steps.say: Warm up: follow the snail into the middle of his shell!
g curls round, then a tail under!
s curves one way, then the other!
j is a line down, a hook, and a dot!
Now write the whole word: goose!

skills.teach: Follow the snail round and round into the middle of his shell!

skills.subject: writing
skills.title: Chicken Crossing
skills.activity: Why did the chicken cross the road? To trace a plus sign!
skills.parentTip: The cross (down, then across) and the two diagonals are the strokes behind t, x, k and the capitals.

steps.say: Warm up: the chicken crosses the road: down, then across!
t is down, then a cross!
x is two slants that cross!
k is a tall line, then a kick!
Now write the whole word: fox!

skills.teach: Why did the chicken cross the road? To trace a plus sign!

skills.subject: writing
skills.title: Pig Pen Shapes
skills.activity: Build the pig a pen, a shark a fin, and the sheep a moon. Trace the shapes!
skills.parentTip: Square and triangle are the last pre-writing shapes. Corners take a stop-and-turn; cheer the corners.

steps.say: Warm up: build the pig a square pen!
Trace the shark's pointy fin!
o is a circle, like the moon!
p is a line down under, then a belly!
Now write the whole word: pig!

skills.teach: Build the pig a pen, a shark a fin, and the sheep a moon. Trace the shapes!

skills.subject: writing
skills.title: Cat Curls
skills.standard: CA CCSS L.K.1a · lowercase c o a d g
skills.activity: The round letters all start like a c. Trace the first letter of each animal!
skills.parentTip: c, o, a, d and g all begin with the same counter-clockwise curl from the top. That's why they're grouped.

steps.say: c is for cat! Start at the top and curl left.
o is for owl! Curl all the way round.
a is for ant! Curl round, then a short line down.
d is for dog! Curl round, then a tall line down.
g is for goat! Curl round, then a tail under.
Now write the whole word: dog!

skills.teach: The round letters all start like a c. Trace the first letter of each animal!

skills.subject: writing
skills.title: Lion Lines
skills.standard: CA CCSS L.K.1a · lowercase l i t k b h
skills.activity: Tall straight letters, top to bottom. Trace the first letter of each animal!
skills.parentTip: These all start with the top-to-bottom line from Giraffe Neck Slide. Line first, then the extra bit.

steps.say: l is for lion! One tall line down.
i is for iguana! A short line and a dot.
t is for turtle! A tall line, then cross it.
b is for bear! Tall line down, then a belly.
h is for horse! Tall line down, then a hump.
k is for kangaroo! Tall line, then a kick.
Now write the whole word: lion!

skills.teach: Tall straight letters, top to bottom. Trace the first letter of each animal!

skills.subject: writing
skills.title: Monkey Humps
skills.standard: CA CCSS L.K.1a · lowercase m n r p u
skills.activity: Hump letters! Down, then up and over. Trace the first letter of each animal!
skills.parentTip: m, n and r are the Over the Barn hump with a line first. u is the hump upside down.

steps.say: m is for monkey! Down, hump, hump.
n is for newt! Down, then one hump.
r is for rabbit! Down, then a little hook.
p is for pig! Down under the line, then a belly.
u is for unicorn! Down, curve, and up.
Now write the whole word: pig!

skills.teach: Hump letters! Down, then up and over. Trace the first letter of each animal!

skills.subject: writing
skills.title: Zebra Zigzags
skills.standard: CA CCSS L.K.1a · lowercase v w x y z
skills.activity: Pointy letters made of slants! Trace the first letter of each animal!
skills.parentTip: These are Fence Hop diagonals. Points at the bottom, not curves.

steps.say: z is for zebra! Across, slant down, across.
v is for vulture! Slant down, slant up.
w is for whale! Down, up, down, up.
y is for yak! Slant down, then a long slant under.
x is for ox! Two slants that cross.
Now write the whole word: yak!

skills.teach: Pointy letters made of slants! Trace the first letter of each animal!

skills.subject: writing
skills.title: Snake Curves
skills.standard: CA CCSS L.K.1a · lowercase s e f j
skills.activity: Curvy letters that slither! Trace the first letter of each animal!
skills.parentTip: The wiggly ones. s is a Duck Pond Wave standing up; e is one Bee Loop.

steps.say: s is for snake! Curve one way, then the other.
e is for elephant! Across, then curl round.
f is for fox! Hook at the top, line down, cross.
j is for jellyfish! Line down, hook, and a dot.
Now write the whole word: fox!

skills.teach: Curvy letters that slither! Trace the first letter of each animal!

skills.subject: writing
skills.title: Big Animal Letters
skills.activity: BIG letters for big animals! Trace the capital that starts each one.
skills.parentTip: Capitals are all top-to-bottom lines, circles and slants: the pre-writing strokes, assembled.

steps.say: L is for Lion!
P is for Parrot!
D is for Duck!
G is for Goat!
H is for Hen!
C is for Cow!
Now write the whole word: Cow!

skills.teach: BIG letters for big animals! Trace the capital that starts each one.

skills.subject: writing
skills.title: Write cow and pig
skills.activity: Write two whole farm words, one letter at a time!
skills.parentTip: A whole word is a big step from single letters. Say each letter with him, then read the word back together.

steps.say: c-o-w. Trace the c!
Now the o!
And the w. That spells cow!
Now write the whole word: cow!
p-i-g. Trace the p!
Now the i!
And the g. That spells pig!
Now write the whole word: pig!

skills.teach: Write two whole farm words, one letter at a time!

skills.subject: writing
skills.title: Write duck and hen
skills.activity: Two more farm words to write, letter by letter!
skills.parentTip: duck has the tricky ck ending. Two letters, one sound.

steps.say: d-u-c-k. Trace the d!
Now the u!
Now the c!
And the k. That spells duck!
Now write the whole word: duck!
h-e-n. Trace the h!
Now the e!
And the n. That spells hen!
Now write the whole word: hen!

skills.teach: Two more farm words to write, letter by letter!

skills.subject: writing
skills.title: Write lion cub
skills.activity: Write the two words that mean YOU: lion cub!
skills.parentTip: He calls himself a lion cub. Writing his own name for himself is the most motivating word there is.

steps.say: l-i-o-n. Trace the l!
Now the i!
Now the o!
And the n. That spells lion!
Now write the whole word: lion!
c-u-b. Trace the c!
Now the u!
And the b. Lion cub!
Now write the whole word: cub!

skills.teach: Write the two words that mean YOU: lion cub!

skills.subject: writing
skills.title: Write parrot
skills.activity: A long word for a talking bird. Write parrot, letter by letter!
skills.parentTip: Six letters is a real word. Notice the double r together.

steps.say: p-a-r-r-o-t. Trace the p!
Now the a!
Now an r!
And another r!
Now the o!
And the t. That spells parrot!
Now write the whole word: parrot!

skills.teach: A long word for a talking bird. Write parrot, letter by letter!

skills.subject: writing
skills.title: Write goat and dog
skills.activity: Two more animals to write!
skills.parentTip: goat has a vowel team (oa). Just trace it; the reading comes later.

steps.say: g-o-a-t. Trace the g!
Now the o!
Now the a!
And the t. That spells goat!
Now write the whole word: goat!
d-o-g. Trace the d!
Now the o!
And the g. That spells dog!
Now write the whole word: dog!

skills.teach: Two more animals to write!

skills.subject: writing
skills.title: Count and Write 1-5
skills.activity: Count the animals, then write the number!
skills.parentTip: Writing the numeral right after counting ties the symbol to the amount.

steps.say: 1 lion! Write the 1.
2 ducks! Write the 2.
3 chicks! Write the 3.
4 goats! Write the 4.
5 pigs! Write the 5.

skills.teach: Count the animals, then write the number!

skills.subject: writing
skills.title: Count and Write 6-10
skills.activity: Bigger herds, bigger numbers. Write each one!
skills.parentTip: 10 is two glyphs; he traces the 1 and then the 0.

steps.say: 6 bees! Write the 6.
7 fish! Write the 7.
8 sheep! Write the 8.
9 cows! Write the 9.
10 hens! Write the 10.

skills.teach: Bigger herds, bigger numbers. Write each one!

family-add.title: Gabriel's Family of 10
family-add.covers: Adding up to 10, one easy step at a time: counting, adding one more, putting two groups together, counting on, number bonds, and making 10. Brand-new questions every time you play.

farm-sort.title: Sort the Farm Animals
farm-sort.covers: Sort the farm animals into their groups (chickens, sheep, cats, and dogs), then see how many are in each. Builds sorting into categories and counting each group (CA CCSS K.MD.B.3).

shapes.title: Shape Detective
shapes.covers: Name and describe flat shapes: circle, square, triangle, rectangle, and hexagon. Find each shape by its name or by how many sides it has (CA CCSS K.G.2).

shape-spot.title: Shape Spotter
shape-spot.covers: Find every triangle, circle, square, rectangle, or hexagon, even when it is big, small, or turned. Names shapes no matter their size or which way they face (CA CCSS K.G.2).

letter-detective.title: Letter Detective
letter-detective.covers: Find letters by their name or by the sound they make. Each letter shows its big and little form, and every answer gives the sound and a key word (CA CCSS RF.K).

weather-watch.title: Weather Detective
weather-watch.covers: Look at the weather and name it: sunny, rainy, cloudy, snowy, windy, or stormy. Find it by name or by what it does, and learn what to wear (CA NGSS K-ESS2-1).

number-detective.title: Number Detective
number-detective.covers: Count the dots and find the number, or read the number and find the matching group. Connects numbers to how many (CA CCSS K.CC.4-5).

american-symbols.title: American Symbols
american-symbols.covers: Find the U.S. flag, the Statue of Liberty, the bald eagle, the Liberty Bell, and the White House, and learn a little about each (CA HSS K.2).

community-helpers.title: Community Helpers
community-helpers.covers: Meet the people who help us: firefighters, police officers, doctors, teachers, farmers, chefs, and builders. Find each helper and learn what they do (CA HSS K.3).

holidays.title: Holidays
holidays.covers: Learn what our holidays celebrate: Thanksgiving, the Fourth of July, MLK Day, New Year's Day, Valentine's Day, and Halloween (CA HSS K.1).

my-family.title: My Family
my-family.covers: Families come in all kinds! Meet Gabriel's family, his two moms Mommy and Maddy plus the cats and dogs, and learn what everyone does at home (CA HSS K.3).

pages.text: Families come in all kinds! 💛 A mom and a dad, two moms, two dads, or grandparents.
This is YOUR family! 🦁 Maddy the Lion, Mommy the Lioness, and you, the Lion Cub! Plus your cats and dogs. 🐱🐶

patterns.title: What Comes Next?
patterns.covers: Look at the repeating color pattern and tap the color that comes next. Builds pattern thinking, an early math skill.

rhyme-time.title: Rhyme Time
rhyme-time.covers: Find the word that rhymes! Cat and hat, dog and frog. Builds the rhyming sound skill that powers reading (CA CCSS RF.K.2a).

flat-or-solid.title: Flat or Solid?
flat-or-solid.covers: Some shapes are flat, like a circle you draw. Some are solid, like a ball you hold. Tell flat (2D) from solid (3D) shapes (CA CCSS K.G.3).

plant-or-animal.title: Plant or Animal?
plant-or-animal.covers: Sort living things by what you can see: which is a plant, which is an animal, which can fly, and which lives in water (CA NGSS K).

bigger-smaller.title: Bigger or Smaller?
bigger-smaller.covers: Compare two things: which is bigger or smaller, taller or shorter, heavier or lighter? Describes and compares size, height, and weight (CA CCSS K.MD.1-2).

build-shape.title: Build a Shape
build-shape.covers: Put simple shapes together to make a picture - a triangle and a square make a house! Finish each picture by tapping the missing shape (CA CCSS K.G.6).

word-problems.title: Story Problems
word-problems.covers: Solve add and subtract story problems you can see: some come, some go away. Find the answer within 20 (CA CCSS 1.OA.1).

push-pull.title: Push or Pull?
push-pull.covers: Things move when we push or pull them. Look at each one and tap how it moves (CA NGSS K-PS2-1).

living-needs.title: What They Need
living-needs.covers: Plants and animals need food, water, and sunlight to live. Tap what each one needs (CA NGSS K-LS1-1).

position-words.title: Where Is It?
position-words.covers: Describe where things are: on top, under, or next to. Tap the picture that matches (CA CCSS K.G.1).

sight-words.title: Star Words
sight-words.covers: Read the words that pop up everywhere: the, and, see, my, like. Find the matching word (CA CCSS RF.K.3c).

number-order.title: More or Less
number-order.covers: What comes next when we count, and which number is more or less? Tap the right number (CA CCSS K.CC.4-6).

animal-homes.title: Animal Homes
animal-homes.covers: Animals live in different places: the farm, the ocean, cold snowy places, and the jungle. Match each animal to its home (CA NGSS K-ESS3-1).

animal-legs.title: How Many Legs?
animal-legs.covers: Count an animal's legs: birds have 2, dogs have 4, bugs have 6, spiders have 8. Counting to tell how many (CA CCSS K.CC.4).

animal-coverings.title: Fur, Feathers, Scales
animal-coverings.covers: Animals are covered in fur, feathers, or scales. Sort each animal by its body covering (CA NGSS 1-LS1-1).

animal-eats.title: What Do Animals Eat?
animal-eats.covers: Every animal eats to live. Match each animal to the food it eats (CA NGSS K-LS1).

teen-numbers.title: Teen Numbers
teen-numbers.covers: Teen numbers are a ten and some more: 13 is ten and three. Count the group of ten plus the extra ones (CA CCSS K.NBT.1).

baby-animals.title: Baby Animals
baby-animals.covers: Baby animals look like their parents, just smaller. Match each parent to its baby (CA NGSS 1-LS3-1).

living-not.title: Alive or Not?
living-not.covers: Living things grow, eat, and move. Tell what's alive (animals and plants) from what's not (toys and rocks) - CA NGSS K.

day-night.title: Day or Night?
day-night.covers: Some animals are awake at night, like owls and bats; others in the day, like bees. Match each animal to when it's awake (CA NGSS day & night patterns).

make-5.title: Make 5
make-5.covers: Find how many more make 5: 3 and 2, 4 and 1. Building the number 5 with two parts (CA CCSS K.OA.4).

which-more.title: Which Has More?
which-more.covers: Count two groups of animals and tap the one with more (or fewer). Comparing quantities (CA CCSS K.CC.6).

egg-or-not.title: Egg or Not?
egg-or-not.covers: Some animals hatch from eggs (hens, turtles, fish); others are born (puppies, calves). Sort animals by how they have young (CA NGSS K).

wild-or-pet.title: Wild or Pet?
wild-or-pet.covers: Pets live with people, like dogs and cats. Wild animals live on their own, like lions. Sort each animal (CA NGSS K).

make-10.title: Make 10
make-10.covers: Some animals are here. Find how many more make ten (CA CCSS K.OA.4).

take-away.title: Take Away
take-away.covers: Some animals hop away. Count how many are left (CA CCSS K.OA.1).

doubles.title: Doubles
doubles.covers: A double is a number and itself. 2 and 2 makes 4 (CA CCSS 1.OA.6).

ordinals.title: First, Second, Third

sun-slept-in.covers: This story covers all 9 Kindergarten reading skills: key details, beginning-middle-end, characters and setting, new words, story vs. poem, author and illustrator, how pictures help, comparing characters, and reading with interest.

pages.text: 🌅 The farm was dark and quiet. Henrietta the 🐔 hen woke up.
"Where is 🐓 Rooster? He crows to wake the ☀️ sun!"
She ran to the 🌱 pasture. 🐐 Maple the goat came to help.
At the 🛖 barn, the 🐕 dogs Bodhi and Kona sniffed for Rooster.
They found 🐓 Rooster asleep 😴 in the 🌾 hay. He overslept!
"Cock-a-doodle-doo! 🐓" The ☀️ sun came up. The farm woke up. 😊

questions.teach: 🐓 Rooster has a BIG job! When he crows, the ☀️ sun comes up and the whole farm 🐮🐷 wakes up.

questions.teach: 🌅 Henrietta woke up at DAWN. Dawn is the early morning time when the ☀️ sun first comes up.
🌱 Henrietta hurried to the PASTURE. A pasture is a big grassy field 🌾 where the animals eat.
🛖 They found Rooster in the HAY LOFT. A hay loft is the space up high at the top of the barn, full of 🌾 hay.
😴 Rooster OVERSLEPT! That means he slept too long ⏰ and missed his job of waking the sun.
📖 A story tells what happens. A 🎵 poem is shorter, and the ending words often rhyme, like a little song.
prompts: What does a poem often do? 🎵
